To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stress hormones enhance the excitability and responsiveness of principal neurons in the basolateral amygdala, a brain region involved in emotional arousal and memory consolidation.
corticosterone (a stress hormone) enhances the excitability of BLA cells by decreasing GABA inhibition and increasing intrinsic excitability.

corticosterone (a glucocorticoid) enhances the excitability of basolateral amygdala (an emotional memory center) neurons by increasing their intrinsic membrane excitability and by reducing the impact of GABAergic inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the facilitatory effects of glucocortiocoids (GC) in memory consolidation.
the mechanisms by which the amygdala participates in the modulation of memory consolidation.
the effects of glucocortocoids on the electrophysiological properties of neurons of the basolateral complex of the amygdaloid complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of stress hormones on BLA neurons, which are the main targets of stress hormones in the amygdala, would be to enhance their excitability.
stress hormones enhance the excitability and responsiveness of principal BLA neurons.
glucocorticoids increase the excitability of BLA neurons and thereby enhance the ability of this nucleus to influence other brain structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucocorticoids facilitate memory consolidation by enhancing the excitability of BLA neurons.
glucocorticoids have a direct effect on the BLA neurons, which is in agreement with the previous behavioral studies, suggesting the involvement of this brain region in the consolidation of memory.
the stress hormone CORT enhances the activity of principal neurons of the BLA, which could facilitate synaptic plasticity in downstream targets of the BLA.

stress hormones can directly alter the activity of BLAs neurons, which could in turn facilitate synaptic plasticity in downstream brain regions.
